text:
**I’d pick the Chase UK current account for everyday debit-card spending if you can comfortably keep £1,000 in Chase savings and make 15 payments a month.** There’s no monthly account fee, and you get **2% cashback** on eligible UK spending, including groceries, cafés, restaurants, takeaways, everyday transport, fuel and public EV charging. Spend £500 a month in those categories and you’d earn **£10 back**; at £1,000 you’d hit the **£20 monthly cap**. Other shopping doesn’t earn cashback. ([which.co.uk](https://www.which.co.uk/reviews/bank-accounts/article/best-bank-accounts/best-bank-accounts-for-cashback-apHnX3k0M1Ui?utm_source=openai))

**The catch:** New customers get cashback for the rest of the month they join and the whole of the next month. After that, eligibility depends on the **previous calendar month**: you must have kept at least £1,000 across your Chase saver accounts **every day** and made at least 15 payments by Chase card or Direct Debit. Money in the current account doesn’t count towards the £1,000. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/legal/cashback-terms-and-conditions/?utm_source=openai))

**If you’d rather not track those conditions, I’d pick Starling instead.** It has no monthly fee, and you can set bill money aside in a separate “Space” and pay bills directly from it. That makes it easy to see what’s actually left to spend. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/current-account/))
